name: PixelLab
summary: AI generator for pixel art game assets: characters, 4/8-direction rotations, text- and skeleton-based sprite animations, tilesets, maps and UI elements.
pricing: Free trial tier (no credit card). Paid plans listed at $12/month (2,000 generations), $24/month (5,000) and $50/month (10,000). API usage priced separately per call.
license: Pricing page lists "Use generated images commercially" and says the user owns the rights to generations, except using them to train models. Terms also reference the Open RAIL-M license.
verdict: For 2D devs who need pixel-art sprites, rotations and animations; outputs are usable commercially on every plan, but its terms bar training other models on them.

name: Retro Diffusion
summary: Pixel-art-specific image models for sprites, tiles, tilesets and animations, plus low-poly 3D model generation with export for Godot, Unity and Unreal. Also sells an Aseprite extension.
pricing: Pay per generation from a prepaid balance: images from $0.03 (RD Fast), $0.06, $0.18 (RD Pro); animations from $0.07 per clip. New accounts get a free starting balance.
license: Official FAQ: "Everything you generate is yours, for personal and commercial projects alike."
verdict: For pixel-art devs who want pay-per-image pricing with no subscription; the site says all output is yours for commercial use.

name: Scenario
summary: Production-focused generative platform for game art: train custom style models on your own assets, generate images, textures, 3D meshes, video and audio. API-first with Unity/Unreal integration.
pricing: Free tier with 50 daily credits. Starter $15/month, Pro $45/month, Max $75/month (monthly billing; annual saves 33%). Enterprise custom.
license: All paid plans include a full commercial license; free plan outputs are for personal and evaluation use only (per pricing FAQ).
verdict: For studios that want custom style models trained on their own art; commercial use needs a paid plan (free output is personal/evaluation only).

name: Leonardo.Ai
summary: General image and video generation platform with trainable custom models; usable for concept art, item icons and texture ideas.
pricing: Free: 150 fast tokens/day (public creations). Essential $12/month, Premium $30/month, Ultimate $60/month (ex. tax). Team and API plans available.
license: Paid subscribers retain full ownership and IP rights. Free tier: Leonardo holds rights to the images but grants you a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence for commercial use; free creations are public.
verdict: For general concept art and icon ideas; free-tier output can be used commercially but is public and Leonardo holds rights to it, while paid plans give you ownership.

name: Layer
summary: Generative content platform aimed at game studios: style-trained models, concept art, marketing creatives and asset variations with team workflows.
pricing: Start for free. Subscriptions begin at $10/month for 300 Creative Units, increasing by $60 per 1,000 CUs; $0 per seat.
license: Pricing page lists "Commercial license for all users". Free-tier scope: unverified.
verdict: For studios that want style-trained generation with no per-seat fees; the pricing page lists a commercial licence for all users.

name: Ludo.ai
summary: Game ideation and asset tool: concept generation, sprites and sprite sheets, textures, plus a Unity editor plugin and API.
pricing: Free plan (sprite sheets watermarked). Indie $15/month ($180/year), Pro $35/month ($420/year), Studio $300/month ($3,600/year); credit packs from $15.
license: FAQ: the person who initiates a generation is recognized as the full owner of that content and can export and use it as they see fit.
verdict: For Unity devs who want ideation and 2D assets in one place; its FAQ says you own what you generate, but free-plan sprite sheets are watermarked.

name: Meshy
summary: Text-to-3D and image-to-3D model generation with AI texturing; paid plans add animation with 600+ motions. DCC bridge listed for Roblox, Blender, Godot, Unity and Unreal.
pricing: Free: 100 monthly credits. Pro $20/month (1,000 credits). Higher tiers listed at $40 and $70 (Studio, team) per month; Enterprise custom.
license: Paid plans: you own the assets you create. Free plan: assets licensed to you under CC BY 4.0 (commercial use with attribution to Meshy).
verdict: For quick text- or image-to-3D props with Godot/Unity/Unreal bridges; free output is CC BY 4.0, so you must credit Meshy unless you pay.

name: Tripo AI
summary: Text/image/multi-view to 3D model generation with retopology, segmentation and up to 4K/8K texture generation. DCC bridge lists Blender, Unity, Unreal, Godot and others.
pricing: Free: 200 monthly credits. Pro $20/month billed annually ($240/yr). Max $90/month billed annually. Team $55/seat/month billed annually.
license: Pricing page: Free plan = "Public Models · Non-Commercial Use"; Pro, Max and Team = "Private Models · Commercial Use".
verdict: For 3D models with retopology and engine bridges; the free plan is non-commercial, so shipping assets requires a paid plan.

name: Hyper3D Rodin
summary: Rodin generates 3D models from text or images, with options like high-poly quad meshes; the platform also lists HDRI and texture generators.
pricing: Free tier ($0; direct credits $1.5 each). Creator $30/month ($24/month yearly). Business $120/month ($96/month yearly). Enterprise custom.
license: Business plan lists "Commercial license included"; FAQ says paid plans include broader export and usage rights. Exact rights on Free and Creator: unverified.
verdict: For high-detail 3D generation; commercial rights on the Free and Creator tiers are unverified, so check its terms before you ship.

name: Sloyd
summary: Template-based and AI 3D generator for game-ready props and objects, with browser editor and plugins for Unity, Unreal and Blender on paid plans.
pricing: Free Guest plan. Plus $15/month ($12.50/month billed yearly). Pro $50/month ($41.67/month billed yearly).
license: Free plan: personal-use license. Plus and Pro include a commercial license (you own what you generate; Pro adds reselling).
verdict: For game-ready props from editable templates with Unity/Unreal plugins; the free plan is personal-use only.

name: Hunyuan3D 2.1 (Tencent)
summary: Open-weights image-to-3D model with PBR material generation that you can run on your own hardware.
pricing: Free to download and self-host (your own GPU/compute costs apply).
license: Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.1 Community License: does NOT apply in the EU, UK or South Korea; use of the works or outputs outside the licensed territory is unauthorized; products with over 1 million monthly active users must request a license from Tencent.
verdict: For devs who can self-host a 3D model generator at no licence cost; the licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea, and products over 1 million monthly users must request a licence.

name: Skybox AI (Blockade Labs)
summary: Generates 360° panoramic skyboxes and environments (up to 16K and HDRI on higher tiers), with an API for in-app generation.
pricing: Essential $20/month, Standard $48/month per seat, Business $112/month (as listed on the plans page; a second set of prices $24/$140 is also shown, likely monthly vs annual billing: unverified). Free tier details: unverified.
license: Terms: "You own all Assets You create with the Services, to the extent possible under current law." Plans page lists "Commercial licensing" on the Business tier; commercial terms for lower tiers: unverified.
verdict: For 360° skyboxes and environment backdrops; the terms say you own your assets, but commercial terms below the Business tier are unverified.

name: Cascadeur
summary: Physics-based keyframe animation software with AI-assisted autoposing, inbetweening and mocap cleanup; exports FBX, DAE, USD and glTF on paid plans.
pricing: Free (non-commercial, .casc export only). Indie $19/month or $8/month billed annually. Pro $49/month or $33/month billed annually. Teams $49/user/month.
license: Free and Educational: no commercial use. Indie: commercial use only if revenue/funding is under $100,000/year. Pro and Teams: full commercial use.
verdict: For hand-keyed character animation with AI posing help; free is non-commercial, and Indie only covers studios under $100k a year in revenue/funding.

name: DeepMotion Animate 3D
summary: Markerless AI motion capture: turns ordinary video into 3D character animation; sister product SayMotion does text-to-motion.
pricing: Freemium (free, no card). Starter $9, Innovator $17, Professional $39, Studio $83 per month, paid annually.
license: Freemium accounts are for personal, non-commercial use; a premium subscription plan is required for licensed (commercial) animation.
verdict: For turning reference video into 3D animation cheaply; the free Freemium tier is non-commercial only.

name: Rokoko Vision
summary: AI motion capture from video plus text-to-motion clips, exported via Rokoko Studio as FBX/BVH for Unity, Unreal, Blender and other tools.
pricing: Starter free (30 seconds of Vision processing per month). Basic $20/month and Plus $50/month (yearly billing). Pro: contact sales.
license: Commercial-use terms for Vision output were not found on the pages checked: unverified.
verdict: For trying video-based mocap for free (30 seconds a month); commercial terms for its output are unverified.

name: Unity AI
summary: AI built into the Unity Editor: an Assistant for project questions and code, plus generators for images, textures, materials, sounds, 3D models and animations, metered in Unity Credits.
pricing: Unity Personal (free) includes a 1,000 monthly Unity Credit allowance; Pro (from $2,310/yr) includes 2,000; Enterprise 3,000. "Special terms apply to Unity Credits." Credits reset monthly and don't roll over.
license: Unity's plans FAQ says you own content you create using Unity; AI-output-specific terms were not checked: unverified.
verdict: For Unity users who want AI inside the editor, with monthly credits included on Personal, Pro and Enterprise plans; AI-output licence terms are unverified.

name: Ludus AI
summary: AI toolkit that runs inside the Unreal Engine editor: an agent that understands your project's Blueprints, C++, assets and levels and can answer questions and make edits.
pricing: 14-day Pro trial. Pro $25/month, Studio $80/month, Ultimate $180/month (plus VAT; yearly billing discounted). Free account has no credits.
license: Ownership/commercial terms for generated output: unverified.
verdict: For Unreal devs who want a project-aware assistant in the editor; it has no free credits beyond a 14-day trial, and its output licence is unverified.

name: GitHub Copilot
summary: AI coding assistant with code completions, chat and agent mode; usable for gameplay code in any engine's scripting language.
pricing: Free plan. Paid individual plans listed at $10, $39 and $100 per month; Business and Enterprise plans for organizations.
license: Copilot Product Specific Terms: "GitHub does not own Suggestions. You retain ownership of Your Code." IP indemnity applies to organization plans, not individual plans.
verdict: For coding in any engine with a free starting tier; GitHub says it doesn't own suggestions, and IP indemnity only comes with organization plans.

name: Cursor
summary: AI-first code editor with agents, chat and codebase-aware edits; usable for gameplay code in any language or engine.
pricing: Free $0/month; Plus $8/month; Premium $30/month; Super $100/month; Ultra $200/month; Teams $30+/user/month. Third-party model usage billed separately.
license: Terms of Service 5.3: you retain rights in Inputs and Anysphere assigns to you all of its right, title and interest (if any) in Suggestions.
verdict: For devs who want an AI-first editor with a free tier; its terms assign suggestion rights to you, and third-party model usage is billed separately.

name: Windsurf
summary: AI code editor with agentic coding and unlimited tab completions on the free plan.
pricing: Free $0/month; Pro $20/month; a $200/month tier; Teams $80/month plus $40/month per full seat.
license: Individual terms 3.1: Cognition assigns to you all right, title and interest in Output.
verdict: For an AI code editor whose free plan includes unlimited tab completions; its terms assign output rights to you.

name: ElevenLabs
summary: Text-to-speech, voices, sound effects and music generation; usable for NPC voice lines and SFX.
pricing: Free $0 (10,000 credits). Starter $6, Creator $22 ($11 first month), Pro $99, Scale $299, Business $990 per month. Enterprise custom.
license: Terms: free-plan users may only use the Services for non-commercial purposes; paid-subscription users may use them commercially (subject to the Prohibited Use Policy).
verdict: For NPC voice lines and SFX; free-plan output is non-commercial, so a paid plan is required to ship.

name: Inworld AI
summary: Realtime text-to-speech and LLM inference platform that can power voiced, interactive characters.
pricing: Free pay-as-you-go ($25 per 1M chars TTS). Subscriptions $25, $100, $300 and $1,500 per month with included credits and lower rates.
license: Terms: subject to compliance, Inworld assigns to you all of its right, title and interest in Outputs. Pricing page also lists a commercial license.
verdict: For realtime TTS and LLM-driven characters on pay-as-you-go pricing; its terms assign outputs to you.

name: Convai
summary: Conversational AI characters for games and virtual worlds: NPCs with voice, knowledge and actions.
pricing: Free $0/month (100 interactions quota). Paid tiers listed at $29, $99, $499 and $1,199 per month (lower discounted figures also shown).
license: Terms of Service: you have ownership over your Customer Content and AI Generated Content.
verdict: For conversational NPCs with a free tier to prototype on; its terms give you ownership of AI-generated content.

name: Charisma.ai
summary: Platform for building interactive stories and AI character conversations, with script flow tools and AI voices, published to web, VR or game engines via SDKs.
pricing: PRO: pay as you go, $5 per 50,000 credits (approx. 200 experience minutes). Enterprise: custom.
license: Terms: the customer (story owner) is deemed owner of Input and Output and Charisma assigns those rights to the customer, subject to its terms.
verdict: For story-driven AI character conversations on pay-as-you-go credits; its terms assign input and output rights to the customer.

name: Suno
summary: Text-to-music generator for full songs and instrumentals; used for prototyping soundtracks and menu music.
pricing: Free $0/month (no commercial rights). Paid plans shown at $12 and $35 per month (yearly-billing savings advertised).
license: Terms: Pro/Premier subscribers are assigned Suno's rights in their Output; free/basic tier Outputs are for personal, non-commercial use only.
verdict: For prototype songs and menu music; free-tier output is personal, non-commercial use only.

name: Udio
summary: AI music generation and remixing app.
pricing: Free $0 (10 credits/day, 100/month). Standard $10/month ($8 billed annually). Pro $30/month ($24 billed annually).
license: Current Terms of Service list exploiting the Services or any Output for any commercial purpose among prohibited uses. Not suitable for shipping in commercial games under these terms.
verdict: For personal music experiments only; its current terms prohibit commercial use of output, so it isn't suitable for shipped games.

name: AIVA
summary: AI composer for soundtrack-style music with MIDI and audio export, editable in its built-in editor.
pricing: Free €0 (3 downloads/month). Standard €11/month (15 downloads). Pro €33/month (300 downloads). Prices shown with annual billing.
license: Free: non-commercial, credit AIVA, copyright owned by AIVA. Standard: limited monetization (YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram only). Pro: copyright owned by you, full monetization.
verdict: For soundtrack-style game music; only the Pro plan gives you the copyright, and the free plan is non-commercial.

name: Stable Audio
summary: Stability AI's text-to-audio tool for generating music and audio clips.
pricing: Free $0 (personal, non-commercial). $12/month (660 credits), $30/month, $90/month, $199/month.
license: Free plan: personal, non-commercial use. Paid plans list a commercial license.
verdict: For generated music and audio clips; the free plan is non-commercial, while paid plans include a commercial licence.

name: SOUNDRAW
summary: Royalty-free AI music generator where you set genre, mood, length and structure and then edit the track.
pricing: Paid plans shown in AUD from our location: A$9.16, A$16.58, A$19.92 and A$27.42 per month. USD prices and free tier: unverified.
license: License page: "All Plans: Personal and commercial use in all of your projects."
verdict: For editable royalty-free background music; its licence page allows commercial use on all plans (USD pricing unverified).

name: Mubert Render
summary: AI-generated royalty-free music tracks by mood, genre and duration, with a track editor.
pricing: Free (non-commercial, 5 downloads/month). Paid plans listed at $14, $39 and $199 per month.
license: Creator plan is non-commercial; commercial use needs Pro or Business, and the pricing FAQ says Business is designed for apps and games. Tracks cannot be redistributed as standalone music.
verdict: For royalty-free background tracks; game use points to the Business plan, and tracks can't be redistributed as standalone music.

name: Beatoven.ai
summary: AI background-music generator; its site lists games among supported uses.
pricing: unverified (pricing page could not be loaded when checked).
license: FAQ: you get a non-exclusive perpetual licence to use and monetise downloaded tracks; Beatoven.ai remains the owner of the tracks.
verdict: For background music you can monetise; you get a perpetual licence but Beatoven keeps ownership, and pricing is unverified.
